title: Emergency Spells break the Spell cadence but not the quality-assurance processes
content:
A.1.10.5.1 defines Emergency Spells as "expedited ad hoc Spells that, while typically compliant with all customary quality-assurance processes, do not adhere to the normal Spell cadence."

The distinction is precise and easy to miss. Acceleration is achieved by dropping the *schedule*, not the *review*. An Emergency Spell is out-of-band, not unvetted — which means the speed gain comes from removing queueing latency rather than from removing safety checks.

The second clause narrows their purpose: Emergency Spells "solve the root issue of an emergency / urgent situation impacting the Protocol." This is what separates them from Standby Spells, which only trigger a pre-built mitigation. The division of labour is that Standby Spells buy time by stopping the bleeding, while the Emergency Spell fixes the cause.

Management is assigned to the Core Facilitator and Core GovOps under the Emergency Response roles, tying an off-cadence capability to named accountable parties rather than to whoever happens to be available.
description: They are ad hoc and expedited, yet typically remain compliant with customary QA; what is sacrificed is scheduling, and they must address the root issue rather than only its symptom.
